statement: With k_i=n, frequencies consisting of equal numbers of nq and −nq give 2^n−binomial(n,n/2) distinct equilibria for even n and 0<q<1. For odd n, append one zero frequency and require 0<q<sqrt(414−66sqrt(33))/16; the count becomes 2^n−binomial(n−1,(n−1)/2). These imply asymptotic ratio one to complex degree, not global optimality.

answer.text: Explicit frequency families yield 2^n−binomial(n,n/2) equilibria for even n and 2^n−binomial(n−1,(n−1)/2) for odd n. The ratio of the maximum real count to 2^n−2 tends to one.

notes:
These are attained lower bounds for the full parameter family; Conjecture 4.14 asserts optimality, not proved here.
